title: Accepted Navajo destination-replacement warning
raw_convention: XML-parsed Android text, U+02BC apostrophes unchanged, no backslashes needed, XML escapes once.

rows.english: The completed image could not replace its destination.
rows.raw: Eʼelyaaígíí: naaltsoos hashtʼeelyaa. Díí naaltsoos doo naaltsoos níwohdę́ę́ʼ kweʼé siłtsoozígíí bichʼą́ąhjiʼ hazlį́į́ʼ da.
rows.value: Eʼelyaaígíí: naaltsoos hashtʼeelyaa. Díí naaltsoos doo naaltsoos níwohdę́ę́ʼ kweʼé siłtsoozígíí bichʼą́ąhjiʼ hazlį́į́ʼ da.
rows.display: Eʼelyaaígíí: naaltsoos hashtʼeelyaa. Díí naaltsoos doo naaltsoos níwohdę́ę́ʼ kweʼé siłtsoozígíí bichʼą́ąhjiʼ hazlį́į́ʼ da.
rows.backtranslation: Image: a file was prepared. This file did not replace the file that was here earlier.

semantic_roles.prepared_substitute: naaltsoos hashtʼeelyaa explicitly says a file was prepared, and Díí naaltsoos refers to that file.
semantic_roles.old_target: Second naaltsoos + níwohdę́ę́ʼ kweʼé siłtsoozígíí identifies a file present at this target earlier.
semantic_roles.replacement_relation: bichʼą́ąhjiʼ follows the old-target nominal; hazlį́į́ʼ is the complete dictionary replacement event predicate.
semantic_roles.failure: doo…da negates replacement. There is no directive to the user and no first-person speaker ambiguity.

rows.confidence: Moderate-to-low authored source-grounded nomination; independent judgment required on complete replacement frame and spatial verb application. No native-human or exact-software-sentence gate.
limits: Factual did-not-replace paraphrases the observed failed operation; it does not reproduce the English could modal.

The replacement sentence expands a complete dictionary singular phrase. Its hazlį́į́ʼ spatial/coming-into-being form is not relabeled a flat-object handling verb; source supports the replacement sense, while explicit digital-file subjects remain authored.

Earlier-presence relative is constructed from an exact temporal particle and an independently attested digital-resource relative. No current retention, nonempty target, finished artwork, successful save, recovery, permission cause or retry promise.
Here is contextually the attempted internal file target, not necessarily an external URI.
Only the target relative uses the singular flat-sheet positional metaphor; no generic colour/value Save command is introduced.
This is not an exact whole published sentence or native-speaker certification. No glyph/layout/runtime or Android build/test validation.

independent_findings.evidence: Independently viewed Wall printed17 both whole page and precise crop: bichʼą́ąhjiʼ is glossed in place of it, and the complete Bichʼą́ąhjiʼ hazlį́į́ʼ clause is glossed it replaced it. Candidate spelling preserves the first acute nasal a and both acute nasal i vowels, removes line-wrap hyphenation, and normalizes apostrophes to U+02BC. This is a finite replacement assertion under negation, not an instruction or a newly generated handling imperative.

Wall printed34 directly gives hashtʼeelyaa, it was prepared; it was made ready. Candidate assigns preparation to naaltsoos and uses the canonical image term as topic. This can cover prepared export bytes or unwrapped image-representation bytes. It does not assert completed artwork, successful save, or full pixel decoding.

The first sentence introduces the prepared file. Díí naaltsoos selects that referent as the next sentence topic/subject. The second naaltsoos plus níwohdę́ę́ʼ kweʼé siłtsoozígíí identifies the previous target, immediately before bichʼą́ąhjiʼ. Young educational grammar printed167–168 explains the relative suffix and postpositions following their related nominal. Combining that rule with Wall’s complete in-place-of replacement clause supports new-file versus old-target order without reversing them. Young–Morgan’s sheep example corroborates replacement vocabulary but, with its different transitive handling predicate and old/new noun sequence, does not independently certify this authored order; it is not the argument-order proof.

hazlį́į́ʼ is not classified here as a flat-sheet handling verb. Its complete dictionary construction has the explicit replacement gloss rather than only a generic location gloss, so using that finite construction for a replacement file is a bounded semantic extension. The cited entry supplies no animate-only restriction. Digital-file nominalization remains authored; no source establishes this entire software sentence or proves it is the standard Navajo filesystem-overwrite idiom.

Wilson printed42 supports níwohdę́ę́ʼ as beforehand/from a previous time. Young–Morgan dictionary4 and7–8 gives the singular flat-flexible stem and siłtsooz positional form. The NMPED source visibly uses siłtsoozígíí for a SharePoint resource and mentions a Word document. That supports the document/file metaphor and exact relative, not an overwrite phrase. The earlier-time adjunct locates target presence before the failed replacement; there is no explicit still-present, nonempty, old-image, retention, recovery or external-provider promise.

Young educational report printed102 explicitly describes doo…da and provides a did-not past-event example; the same page notes time-adverb tense reference. Candidate negates the finite replacement clause. Factual did not replace is a functional paraphrase of the observed failed operation, not a literal translation of English could not and not a claim about the user’s willingness or ability.

caller_review.method: Read production files in the supplied synthetic checkout without changing them; recomputed all104 production SHA256 and Git blob identities and inspected all32 resource-only bridges. The checkout HEAD is synthetic and was not used as current remote authority.
caller_review.export: ClassicPaintActivity1363 creates the existing internal target before1364 ImageExporter.encode. The latter routes BMP/GIF,DIB,ICO,Base64 and ASCII to the four throw sites. Each temporary representation writer returns and closes before renameTo failure. The external URI is opened only afterward at1365. The previous target may be empty.
caller_review.classic_import: ClassicPaintActivity1271–1290 creates and copies the cached input then starts ImportSelection. ImportSelection31–32 and53 normalizes that same existing file; decodeToFile(file,file) reads it, writes and closes unwrapped bytes, then only signature-checks them before the replacement attempt.
caller_review.assembly_import: AssemblyActivity235 alone is path construction, not existence evidence. Successful ImportFiles.copy at243 opens and writes destination.outputStream, and start at260 reaches normalization/read of that file. Thus earlier target existence is established for this separate import route too.

Destination often means internal staging target, not the selected external URI.
